rawFindings.title: Property key not converted to string in readObject leading to potential key type issues
rawFindings.explanation: In the readObject function at new line 415, the key variable is converted to a string explicitly via key = key.toString();. This change fixes potential issues where map keys from deserialization may not be strings (e.g., numbers or objects), which can cause inconsistent behavior when using the keys as object properties. Without this fix, keys that are not strings may cause unexpected results or errors when accessing properties on resulting objects.
rawFindings.suggestion: Keep the explicit conversion of keys to strings with key = key.toString(); to ensure consistent property keys in the deserialized object.

rawFindings.title: Risky modification: converting map keys to string in v1 decoder readObject
rawFindings.explanation: The changed line converts all object keys to string by calling key.toString(), which alters keys that were originally numbers or other object types into strings. This diverges from the original behavior where keys retained their type, potentially affecting code that depends on key types such as numeric keys in maps. No tests have been added or updated to verify this behavior change.
rawFindings.suggestion: Remove or justify the forced key.toString() conversion. If string keys are required, explicitly clarify this behavior and add tests to cover scenarios with non-string keys to prevent unexpected side effects.
